label: token right after an early 0 (step 3-4), with x/g/q/u prefix
explanation: Very sparse (about 240 activations in 1M sequences) conjunction feature in the original phase. Nearly all activations (94% of mass) are on the step right after the digit 0, when that 0 is the 3rd or 4th original token (t=3 or 4, rarely 5). It only fires when the tokens before the 0 come from a small set: first token x or g (also 3/u/t/y), token before the 0 q/g/u (also 0/p). The current token is usually l, b or d (also j, y, 2, or <DEL> at the delimiter step). The strongest activations (0.15-0.17) are on prefixes like x g u 0 l, x g g 0 b, g q 0 l. Weaker ones have only one x/g/q/u in the prefix (e.g. y g 0 d, 3 y 0 0 b). It never fires in the copy phase, at t<3, or after a 0 later in the sequence. prev_tok==0 at t in {3,4} alone gets 93% recall but precision 0.3%. Adding the token-identity conditions raises precision to about 20% (dev F1 0.33). The feature looks like a specific lookup over a combination of tokens, not a clean concept.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 36 cues. Raise it: orig0=x (+2.84), prev2_tok=q (+2.68), t=3 & prev_tok=0 (+2.58), prev2_tok=g (+2.04), prev_tok=0 (+2.00), prev2_tok=u (+1.74). Lower it: in_first=0 (-1.92), n_digits=0 (-1.73), in_count=1 (-1.01), to_go=0 (-0.42).
